FOREWORD 


This Indian Standard (First Revision) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by 
the Man-made Fibres, Cotton and their Products Sectional Committee had been approved by the Textiles Division 
Council. 


Polyester staple fibre (PSF) is a manufactured fibre in which the fibre forming substance is any long-chain 
synthetic polymer composed of at least 85 percent by weight of an ester of a substituted aromatic carboxylic acid, 
including but not restricted to substituted terephthalic units, p(-R-O-CO-C,H,-CO-O-)x and para-substituted 
hydroxy-benzoate units, p(-R-O-CO-C,H,-O-)x. PSF made directly from purified terephthalic acid (PTA) and 
mono ethylene glycol (MEG) or polyester (PET) chips is known as ‘virgin fibre’ and that made from recycled 
PET flakes, POPCORN, PET limps, PET wiry waste etc. is known as recycled fibre. 


This standard was first published in 2019 and has been revised to incorporate following changes: 
a) Requirement and test method for identification of material has been modified; 
b) All amendments have been incorporated; 
c) Table for physical requirements of polyester staple fibres has been modified; 
d) Table for chemical and other requirements of polyester staple fibres has been modified; 
e) Marking and packing clause has been modified; and 
f) References to Indian Standards have been updated. 
The composition of the Committee responsible for the formulation of this standard is given in Annex M. 


For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with the final value, 
observed or calculated expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with 
IS 2 : 1960 ‘Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised )’. The number of significant places retained in the 
rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. 


IS 17263 : 2022 


Indian Standard 


TEXTILES — POLYESTER STAPLES FIBRES — 
SPECIFICATION 


( First Revision ) 


1 SCOPE 


1.1 This standard specifies requirements for all types 
of polyester staple fibres (PSF), such as virgin fibres, 
recycled fibres, dope dyed fibres, cationic dyeable 
fibres; and other polyester specialty fibres, such as 
spun lace fibres; slick fibres: antimicrobial fibres; 
nonwoven/filling fibres; flame retardant fibres; 
siliconised fibres and micro fibres; etc. for various end 
usages. 


1.2 Requirements for fibres for use in cement matrix for 
construction works are separately specified in IS 16481 
and are not covered in this standard. 


2 REFERENCES 


The standards listed in Annex A contain provisions, 
which through reference in this text, constitute 
provisions of this standard. At the time of publication, 
the editions indicated were valid. All standards are 
subject to revision and parties to agreements based 
on this standard are encouraged to investigate the 
possibility of applying the most recent editions of the 
standards indicated in Annex A. 


3 TERMS AND DEFINITIONS 


For the purpose of this standard, the following 
definitions shall apply. 


3.1 Cationic Dyeable Polyester — Polyester, modified 
chemically to make it receptive to cationic dyes. 


3.2 Crimp — The waviness of fibre. 


3.3 Crimp Frequency — The number of crimps per 
unit of length of staple fibre. 


3.4 Cross Section — The image of the sliced end in a 
microscope when a single fibre is cut perpendicular to 
the axis 


NOTE — The shape of man-made fibres can be influenced by 
the spinning process and subsequent processing and treatments. 


3.5 Commercial Allowance — A defined percentage 
to be added to the oven-dry mass of the fibre for the 
calculation of commercial mass and certain other 
properties. This allowance includes the moisture 


content and the content of the substances which can 
be removed during analysis, for example, spin finish, 
oligomers etc. 

NOTE — The commercial allowance for Polyester Staple 


Fibre (PSF) shall be 2.0 percent. However, for hygroscopic 
fibres it shall be 15 percent. 


3.6 Commercial Mass — The mass obtained by 
adding to the oven-dry mass, the mass corresponding 
to the commercial allowance. 


3.7 Oven-dry Mass — The mass obtained by drying 
the polyester staple fibre usually after removal of added 
products, such as finish, oil and extractable matters. 


3.8 Dope Dyed Fibres — Fibres manufactured by 
introducing dye (or pigment) into the molten polymer. 


3.9 Dry Heat Shrinkage (Hot Air Shrinkage) — 
The decrease in length of a test specimen caused by 
a treatment in a hot air oven at 180 °C for 30 min, 
expressed as a percentage of the length of the untreated 
test specimen. The lengths are measured before (under 
a specified pretension) and after treatment (under a 
specified measuring tension).

5 IDENTIFICATION AND DESCRIPTION 


5.1 The material, that is polyester, shall be identified by 
confirmatory tests either as per: 
a) Microscopic and dissolution test given in IS 667 
and melting point of 245 °C, Min when tested as 
per method specified in Annex J of IS 16481; or 


b) Staining tests given in IS 667. 
5.2 The polyester staple fibres shall be described using 
the classification (see 4), fibre linear density (denier) 


and other applicable special characteristics as given in 
Table 2. 


6 REQUIREMENTS 


6.1 The polyester staple fibre shall meet the physical 
and chemical requirements as specified in Tables 2 


IS 17263 : 2022 


to 5 and clauses 6.1.1, 6.1.2, 6.2, 6.3 to 6.5 and 6.6 
(optional). 


6.1.1 Polyester staple fibres shall normally be available in 
0.6, 0.8, 1.0, 1.1, 1.2, 1.3, 1.4, 1.5, 1.7, 2.0, 2.2, 3.0, 3.3, 
4.0, 6.0, 7.0 and 15.0 deniers etc. and cut lengths of 6 mm, 
12 mm, 18 mm, 22 mm, 32 mm, 34 mm, 38 mm, 40 mm, 
44 mm, 51 mm, 64 mm, 76 mm, 102 mm, 128 mm etc. 
unless specifically asked for in the contract or order. The 
tolerance on denier and cut length and CV percentage on 
denier shall be as specified in Table 3. 

NOTE — Cut lengths of 32, 38, 44 and 51 mm are generally 


used for cotton spinning and a blend of 76, 88 and 102 mm 
(average cut length of 88 mm) is used for worsted spinning. 


6.2 Freedom from Major Defects 


The polyester fibre shall be free from the following 
major defects (see also 9.3.2). 


6.2.1 Dirt/Grease — No soiling or grease spots shall be 
allowed on fibres. 


6.2.2 Damaged/Bumped Fibres — None allowed. 


6.2.3 Finish Oil Contamination — The fibres shall 
not be contaminated with foreign material of finish oil 
when viewed under microscope or a packing table UV 
light, unless very slight (not immediately visible). Strip 
to clean if possible. Otherwise, reject to off grade. 


6.2.4 Uneven Fluorescent Oil — If applicable, the 
package(s) having uneven coverage under UV light 
shall not be allowed. 


6.2.5 Slubs/Loops/Kinks — None shall be allowed. 


6.2.6 Other Foreign Materials — Such as metals, 
plastic, dust, hair etc. shall not be allowed. 


6.3 Lustre/Brightness 


The polyester staple fibres shall be classified as full dull, 
semi dull, semi dull optically bright, bright, optically 
bright or super bright on the basis of lustre and shall 
meet the requirements specified in Table 5 when tested 
by the method prescribed in Annex L.

6.4 Colour Fastness Properties 


The dyed fibres shall meet the respective colour fastness 
requirements as specified in Table 6. 


6.5 Commercial Mass 


The commercial mass shall be obtained by adding mass 
corresponding to commercial allowance of 2.0 percent 
to the oven dry mass of the consignment when tested by 
the methods prescribed in IS 7703 (Part 3) and it shall 
not be less than the declared commercial mass of the 
consignment. 

NOTE — The commercial allowance may be up to 

15.0 percent in some specific hygroscopic fibres, duly 

mentioned in such cases. 


6.6 Additional 
(Optional) 


For Ecomark, the product shall also comply with the 
additional requirements as given in Table 7. 


Requirements for Ecomark 


IS 17263 : 2022 


7 PACKING 


The polyester staple fibres (PSF) shall be packed in the 
form of bales of 275 kg or as required by the buyer, 
with woven fabric stitched at sides, top and bottom and 
properly strapped using polypropylene/PET straps to 
ensure that the contents are safe from weather, dirt, dust 
and water etc. 


8 MARKING 


8.1 Each bale of polyester staple fibres (PSF) shall be 
marked with indelible ink, the following information: 


a) Name and description of the material (see 4.6 
and 5.1); 


b) Commercial mass of each bale of fibres; 


c) Manufacturer’s name, address and trade-mark 
(if available); 


d) Lot/batch/merge number; 
e) Month and year of manufacture; and 


f) Any other information required by the law in 
force. 


8.1 1 BIS Certification Marking 


The product(s) conforming to the requirements of 
this standard may be certified as per the conformity 
assessment schemes under the provisions of the 
Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016 and the Rules 
and Regulations framed thereunder, and the product(s) 
may be marked with the Standard Mark.

9 SAMPLING AND 
CONFORMITY 


CRITERIA FOR 


9.1 Lot 


The number of bales (see 7.1) of the same description 
and designation delivered to a buyer against one 
dispatch note shall constitute a lot. 


9.2 The number of bales to be selected at random 
from a lot shall be according to col 3 of Table 8. The 
bales shall be selected at random from to constitute the 
sample size. To ensure the randomness of selection, 
IS 4905 may be followed. 


9.2.1 Preparation of Homogeneous Fibre Sample for 
Tests 


The main object of this procedure is to prepare and 
ensure the best average sample for test which will 
represent the product for various quality tests. 


9.2.2 Preparation of Test Sample for Denier and Tensile 
tests 


Requirement Method of Test 
(3) (4) 
20 IS 14563 (Part 1) and IS 14563 (Part 2) 
Annex A of IS 15651 
0.1 
0.1 
Not Detected 
0.2 
0.1 
25 
30 
0.5 Annex B of IS 15651 
1.0 Annex D of IS 15651 
Not Detected Annex D of IS 15651 
20 IS 15570 


9.2.2.1 Follow the procedure described from i) to vi) 
given below: 


a) From the sample available for testing, pick up a 
handful of sample; 


b) Hold the sample using both hands and break open 
the sample by moving hands away from each 
other; 


c) Join both ends and hold the sample in left hand; 


d) Using thumb and forefinger pullout one tuft from 
the open surface and keep it on the table; 


e) Rotate sample in hand and repeat steps 1i) to iv); 
and 


f) Repeat steps i) to v) till the whole sample is 
exhausted. 


9.2.2.2 Combine all the tufts to form a sub sample. 
Blend the sub sample by hand, and using both hands 
break open the sample as described in step ii). Join 
both the ends and hold it in left hand. Using thumb and 
fore finger, pull out tufts by repeated drawing to get 
a specified weight. During the test remove uncut and 
bunches. 


9.2.3 Preparation of Sample for Dry Heat Shrinkage 
(DHS), Crimps per Centimetre (CPCM) and Cut 
Length Properties 


Take a bale sample which is to be tested for CPCM, 
DHS and Cut Length properties and spread on a table. 
Pick-up ten crimped fiber clusters randomly from 
different portions of the sample place on velvet board 
for testing 


9.2.4 Preparation of Sample for Colour 


Take the bale sample which is to be tested for colour, 
take randomly from four or five places a handful of 
sample. Blend it by hand and then air blend in an air 
blender using clean compressed instrument air. 


9.2.5 Preparation of Homogeneous Sample 


Take 100 to 150 g fibre sample from a bale. Divide the 
sample in to eight parts and keep on a surface. Break 
open each part by holding with both hands and the 
outer fibres about 5 g are taken out and discard the left 
over fibre sample. Take specimen from two parts of the 
test sample. The fibres thus obtained from sample Part 
2 is kept on that obtained from Part 1 and break open 
the sample and take out the outer fibres taking care that 
the fibre is not stretched. Thus, one sample is obtained 
from part | and 2. The doubling and dividing process is 
repeated for Part 3 and 4, 5 and 6, 7 and 8, to get four 
samples out of eight. By repeating the same doubling 
and dividing procedure. Two samples are obtained from 
these four samples. Finally, one sample is obtained 
from the last two samples by the same procedure which 
is taken for analysis of tensile properties 


IS 17263 : 2022 


9.3 Number of Tests and Criteria for Conformity 


9.3.1 The number of bales to be selected for testing all 
requirements except resistance to acids/alkalis/ageing 
and UV resistance shall be in accordance with column 
3 of Table 8. For resistance to acids/alkalis/ageing and 
UV resistance, the number of bales selected shall be 
in accordance with column 5 of Table 8. These bales 
may be selected from the bales selected before as per 
column 3. 


9.3.2 All the bales selected from the lot shall be visually 
examined for major fibre defects as specified in 6.2. A 
bale shall be considered defective if it contains any 
major defect. All the samples as prepared in accordance 
with 9.3 above shall be tested for all the requirements 
as specified in 6.1 and 6.3 to 6.6 as applicable. 


9.3.3 The lot shall be declared conforming to the 
requirements of this standard if the total number of 
defective bales does not exceed the value given in 
column 4 of Table 8 for major fibre defects and all other 
requirements except resistance to acids/alkalis/ageing 
and UV resistance or column 6 of Table 8 for resistance 
to acids/alkalis/ageing and UV resistance tests.

ANNEX B 
( Table 3 ) 
MEASUREMENT OF HOLLOWNESS OF HOLLOW FIBRES 


B-1 PRINCIPLE 


This method covers the determination of void content 
in hollow fibres using a microscope and camera. 


B-2 APPARATUS 


a) Optical/polarising microscope 
magnification; 


with proper 


b) PC with image software and interface with 
microscope and camera; 


c) Metallic slides with 
preparation; and 


slot for cross section 


d) Sharp razor blades. 
B-3 SAFETY 


Take care while cutting fibres for cross section 
preparation using sharp edge razor blade. 


B-4 PROCEDURE 


Select small fibre tufts from different portions of the 
fibre sample. Put a small bunch of fibre in to the slit 


of the metallic slide. Cut both sides of the fibre bunch 
with a sharp blade in one cut taking care that the middle 
portion is not disturbed. Put the cross section slide on 
the microscope with proper magnification and light 
source at bottom. Adjust the settings of the microscope 
to get a clear image on the computer screen. Using the 
image analysis software capture the image. Individually 
select carefully by drawing out line on the periphery 
of at least fifteen different single fibre specimen cross 
sections for area measurement. Measure the total area 
of the individual cross section as well as the area of 
the corresponding inside hollow portion and go on 
recording. 


B-5 CALCULATION 


Area of hollow portion x100 
Total cross sectional area 


Hollowness, percent = 


Take the Average of all 15 readings and report. 


ANNEX C 
( Table 3 ) 
DETERMINATION OF CRIMP PROPERTIES 


C-1 PRINCIPLE 


Crimp properties include crimp number, crimp removal 
and crimp stability. This method for determination 
of crimps is applicable to all type of crimps having 
two-dimensional sine-wave configurations. The exact 
numbers of crimps are counted on a particular length of 
a single fibre under proper magnification. Then the fibre 
is straightened without deformation till crimps are just 
removed. The numbers of crimps are expressed per unit 
extended length. Crimp stability is calculated in second 
step by noting down the change in lengths occurring on 
the fibre after loading it with a crimp removal load and 
subsequently withdrawing the load. 


C-2 APPARATUS 


a) Crimp balance; 

b) Forceps; 

c) Velvet board; 

d) Pretension weight; and 
e) Supplementary weight. 


11 


C-3 SAFETY 


There is no safety hazard, however proper illumination 
and magnifying glass is very much required for 
counting crimps on fibre. Activity involves Stress on 
eyes, hence periodic job rotation is required. 


C-4 SAMPLING 


Sampling is done as per the defined testing schedule. 
Take 50 to 100g sample and physically examine 
by spreading the sample on a work table. Pick up 
20 fibres up at random from different fibre chips 
properly representing the whole sample. Condition 
the sample in lab atmosphere for at least 24 hours 
(see IS 6359). 


C-5 PROCEDURE 


C-5.1 Determining the Crimp Number or Crimp 
Frequency 


Check the balancing of the beam of crimp balance. 
Spread the test sample on the table. Pick up fibre 


IS 17263 : 2022 


clusters at random from different places ensuring proper 
representation of the sample. Set the test length to 
20 mm on crimp balance and attach the crimp removal 
load (50 mg/den) on the left side arm of the crimp 
balance. Pick up one fibre specimen from each fibre 
tuft as prepared using forceps. Place these specimens 
on a specimen board and using fingertip pressure flatten 
each specimen with the crimps in a plane parallel to the 
board taking care that the crimps are not disturbed. To 
the one end of test specimen attach a paper gum tag 
(very light weight just to hold the fibre). Grip the free 
end of the specimen with tweezer and clamp it in the 
upper clamp and lower end in lower clamps (end where 
paper gum tag is attached). Count the number of peaks, 
against the contrasting background with vertical line. 
Record the number of peaks. Use magnifying glass 
(a low magnification not more than 10x) with 
illumination for counting. Now unlock the balancing 
arm of crimp balance to release the beam and set 
0.0 on the scale of the micrometer. Set the speed of 
lower clamp to 0.5 to 1.0 mm/s by regulator (to be preset 
by using stop watch during installation of instrument. 
In routine analysis this step is not required). Set motor 
switch to lower position for downward travel. 


C-5.1.1 Stopping is automatic at crimp removal load, 
and the green pilot light will glow. The crimp removal 
load is selected such that it just straightens the fibre 
without any deformation. On releasing the load crimps 
are recovered partly on the fibre confirming that the 
fibre is not stretched. 


C-5.1.2 Record the reading on the micrometer scale 
correct to 0.01 mm (C, extension). 


C-5.2 Determining the Crimp Removal and Crimp 
Stability 


Declamp lower end of specimen and lock the beam. 
Set motor switch for upward travel and keep pressing 
the switch until the motor stop on return to zero on the 
micrometer. Swing lower clamp out of the way and 
clamp 50 mg per denier pretension weight at lower 
end freely for one minute (see table for hanging of pre 
tension weight as per denier). Remove loading weight 
and let specimen allow recovering for one min. Clamp 
the lower end of specimen in the lower clamp and 
release the beam. Repeat above steps and record the 


12 


C, extension of specimen. Similarly test the remaining 
specimen. Report the average along with CV percent. 


C-6 CALCULATIONS 


Calculate the crimp removal percent by the formula: 


(No. of peaks x10) 
(Extended length in mm)x2 


Crimps per cm (CPCM) = 


(Percent C, x100)

C-7 CALIBRATION 


Only standard pre tension weights are used and the 
uncertainty due to the mass is calculated from repeat 
measurement of the weights on a calibrated balance. 
Calibrate the vernier scale for crimp removal length 
measurement with standard vernier caliper and the 
uncertainty of measurement is calculated from the 
standard deviation of repeated measurement.

ANNEX D 
( Table 3 ) 
DETERMINATION OF SINKING TIME FOR SPUNLACE FIBRES 


D-1 PRINCIPLE 


The purpose of the sinking test is to check uniformity 
of spin finish application on the surface of fibres. 


D-2 APPARATUS 
a) Stop-watch; 
b) Weighing balance; 
c) Forceps; and 
d) Beaker, 500 ml. 
D-3 PROCEDURE 


Take approximately 20 g of fibres sample from different 
places and open it in air blender. Weigh exactly 


1.0 g of opened fibres and make spherical shape ball 
(3-4 cm diameter) with hand. Hands should be clean 
and dry before making spherical shape fibre ball. 
Repeat the step for making 5 such spherical shape fibre 
balls of similar volume of given sample. Add 500 ml 
of demineralised water in 500 ml beaker and take one 
spherical shape sample ball; drop it into the beaker 
slowly and simultaneously start the stop watch. Stop 
the stop watch as soon as fibre ball sinks in water and 
note the time taken. Remove the wet fibres from beaker 
and adjust the water level to 500 ml and determine the 
sinking time all the 5 fibre balls of given sample. Now 
calculate the average, minimum, maximum and percent 
coefficient of variation (CV percent) of 5 readings and 
express the result in seconds. 


ANNEX E 
( Table 4 ) 
METHOD FOR DETERMINATION OF MOISTURE REGAIN 


E-1 PRINCIPLE 


The specimen is conditioned in the standard atmosphere, 
weighed, oven dried, weighed again and the moisture 
content is calculated. From this, the moisture regain is 
calculated and expressed as a percentage. 


E-2 APPARATUS 

E-2.1 Precision Balance 
E-2.2 Stainless Steel Vessels 
E-2.3 Forceps 


E-2.4 Hot Air Oven — Capable of maintaining at 
110+5°C. 


E-3 CONDITIONING OF SAMPLES 


The samples shall be allowed to condition at temperature 
of 27 + 2 °C and a relative humidity of 65 + 2 percent 
before carrying out the tests. All tests shall also be 
performed under standard conditions (see IS 6359). 


E-4 PROCEDURE 


Weigh the yarn skein before the test (W,) and dry in the 
oven at a temperature of 110+ 5 °C. After thirty minutes 
weigh the sample and record its mass. Subsequently 
carry out the weighing every twenty minutes until a 
constant mass (W,) is obtained. Calculate the moisture 
content using the relations: 


W=W-W, w (1) 
100xW 
W, 


Moisture content, percent = 


E-5 CALCULATION 

E-5.1 Calculate the moisture regain by the following 
formula: 

Moisture regain, percent = 


Moisture content. percent x100 


100 — Moisture content, percent 


IS 17263 : 2022 


ANNEX F 
( Table 4) 
DETERMINATION OF PHOSPHORUS CONTENT 


F-1 INTRODUCTION 


This method is applicable to determine phosphorus 
content in polymer by colorimetry. Phosphorous 
present in polymer sample is converted to water soluble 
orthophosphate form. This solution is then reacted with 
ammonium molybdate to form molybdo phosphoric 
acid complex. This complex is reduced to blue colour 
by sodium sulfite. Intensity of this complex is measured 
at 710 nm using ultraviolet-visible spectrophotometer. 


F-2 PURPOSE 


a) Phosphorous additives are added during 
polymerization to control thermal degradation. 


b) Phosphrous is added for flame retardant properties 
also. 


F-3 REAGENTS 


F-3.1 10 Percent Sulfuric Acid Solution 
(2 litres) — Add 100 ml of sulfuric acid in 2 000 ml 
beaker containing 500 ml demineralized water, cool the 
beaker to room temp and filter. Transfer the contents 
to 1 000 ml flasks and make up the volume with 
demineralized water. 


F-3.2 5 Percent Ammonium Molybdate Solution 
(500 ml) — Weigh 25 g of ammonium molybdate 
and add to the 500 ml volumetric flask containing of 
10 percent sulphuric acid; dissolve the salt then make 
upto the mark using 10 percent sulphuric acid solution 
(filter if necessary). 


F-3.3 0.5 Percent Hydroquinone Solution 
(500 ml) — Weigh 2.5 g of hydroquinone and to the 
500 ml volumetric flask containing 5 ml of 1 N sulfuric 
acid; dissolve the salt then make up to the mark using 
demineralized water (filter if necessary). 


F-3.4 20 Percent Sodium Sulphite Solution 
(500 ml) — Weigh 100 g of sodium sulphite and add 
to the 500 ml volumetric flask containing 300 ml of 
demineralized water; dissolve the salt then make up to 
the mark using demineralized water (filter if necessary). 


F-3.5 Zine Oxide Solution (200 ml) — Dissolve 
20 g of zinc oxide in 200 ml of 10 percent sulphuric 
acid solution (filter if necessary). 


F-3.6 Whatman Filter Paper No. 1 


14 


F-4 PROCEDURE 


F-4.1 Preparation of Standard Solutions 


Weigh 5.742 g of Di-sodium hydrogen ortho phosphate 
dihydrate and add to the 1 000 ml volumetric flask 
containing 150 ml of 10 percent sulphuric acid; dissolve 
the salt then make up to the mark using demineralized 
water. From the above flask 25 ml of solution is taken 
out in 250 ml volumetric flask and make up to the mark 
using demineralized water, this will give 100 ppm 
standard solution of phosphorus. From the above flask 
of 100 ppm solution, 10 ml of solution is taken out in 
100 ml volumetric flask and make up to the mark using 
demineralized water, this will give 10 ppm std. solution 
of phosphorus. This solution is taken for calibration 
purpose (liquid phosphorous standard). 


F-5 CALIBRATION STANDARD SOLUTION 


From the liquid phosphorous standard solution made 
above, take 2.5, 5, 7.5, 10 and 15 ml solution in 
100 ml standard volumetric flasks and add 20 ml zinc 
oxide solution to each flask. This will correspond to 
0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1, 1.5 ppm of phosphorous solution. 
Plot the graph for concentration in mg of phosphorous 
in 100 ml (X axis) versus Abs (Y axis). Calculate the 
slope factor (SF) from graph (y = mx + c). 


F-6 ANALYTICAL PROCEDURE 


F-6.1 Weigh 1 to 1.5 g polyester chips/yarn sample 
for low content phosphrous expected ~ 10 to 50 ppm. 
For higher contents expected 6 000 to 7 000 ppm 
as phosphorus, sample weight to be taken around 
0.1 g in silica crucible. Keep on hot plate at 150 °C for 
20 min for shrinking. Remove the crucible and cool it. 
Add 1.5 g of zinc oxide over the polymer sample to 
cover it. Keep the crucible on hot plate at 250 to 280 °C 
for 20-30 min, and then add 0.5 g of zinc oxide again 
in hot condition. Keep the silica crucible in furnace at 
600 °C for 60 min (sample will turn into white-yellowish 
mass) then remove the silica crucible and cool. 


F-6.2 Add 20 ml of 10 percent sulphuric acid to the 
sample in silica crucible and dissolve the sample. 
Keep the sample silica crucible on the hot plate at 
100 °C for 10 min (till it become clear solution), cool the 
solution. Filter the sample solution from silica crucible 
if solution is not clear using Whatman filter paper no. 1. 


Collect the filtrate in 100 ml standard volumetric flask. 
Add reagents mentioned in F-6.3. Dilute up to the mark 
with demineralized water. If expected phosphorus is 
7000-8 000 ppm then dilute the solution to 100 ml with 
demineralized water and from this solution take 10 ml 
solution (10 times dilution is done due to high level of 
phosphorus) and add 18 ml of zinc oxide solution and 
then add reagents mentioned in F-6.3 to it. 


F-6.3 Add following solution to each 100 ml standard 
volumetric flask as per the sequence given below: 

a) 10 ml ammonium molybdate; 

b) 5 ml sodium sulphite; and 

c) 5 ml hydroquinone. 


F-6.4 Make up to 100 ml with demineralized water. Take 
two 100 ml volumetric flasks (labeled as A and B). In A, 


IS 17263 : 2022 


add 5ml of liquid phosphorus standard and B use as a 
blank. Add 20 ml zinc oxide solution to each flask Add 
reagents mentioned in F-6.3 to it. Stopper and shake all 
the flasks, keep the flask in dark for 60 min. Take the 
absorbance reading in ultraviolet spectrophotometer at 
710 nm using 50 mm cuvette. 


F-7 CALCULATION 
Phosphorus content, ppm = 


Absorbance x 1000xDilution factor (if any) 
Sample weight (Slope factor) 


Slope factor = 10/Slope (of the graph of absorbance 
versus concentration (mg/ml). 


Report phosphorous content of the sample in ppm. 


ANNEX G 
( Table 4 ) 


MEASUREMENT OF PERCENT SILICONE ON FIBRE BY X-RAY FLUORESCENCE 
SPECTROMETER (XRF) 


G-1 PRINCIPLE 


Silicon percent in polyester is measured on X-ray 
fluorescence spectrometer. Pellet of polyester fibre is 
scanned on X-ray which directly gives concentration 
of elements. 


G-2 APPARATUS AND REAGENTS 


a) X-ray fluorescence spectrometer (XRF); 
b) P-10 carrier gas; 

c) Sample pellet; and 

d) Standard sample for calibration. 


G-3 POTENTIAL SAFETY AND HEALTH 
ISSUES 


XRF Unit — There is no potential safety and 
occupational health issue as such because radiation 
safety is well taken care of by the inherent highly 
standard safety features of the instrument through the 
use of shielding and interlocks, the operator is fully 
protected from any radiation hazard. High voltage 
electrical points are guarded by covers in the case 
and in no situation the cover is removed during the 
operation. ELCB and fuses etc. are provided on the live 
and neutral lines. 


15 


G-4 PREPARATION OF SAMPLE 


Prepare the sample by pressing fibre sample in carver 
hydraulic press by simultaneous application of heat and 
pressure. 


G-5 OPERATION OF PELLET PRESS 


Take 8-10 g of siliconised fibre sample and put into the 
die of pellet. Place the plunger inside the diameter and 
place in the proper place of carver press. Program the 
instrument for 10T/20T pressure, 250 °C temperature 
and for proper residential time setting. Remove the 
pellet after cooling. Condition the pellet for 5-7 min 
and measure for percentage Si on XRF. 


G-6 PROCEDURE 


G-6.1 Measurement of SiO, on XRF 


Prior to measurement standardize the instrument 
with standard sample pellets of known SiO, content 
of different levels and of similar sample symmetry. 
Switch on the instrument and check the parameters for 
vacuum, career gas, voltage, X-ray tube etc. Open the 
measurement program on the PC. Put the sample pellet 
in the sample holder, close the lid. Start Read button. 
Read percentage SiO, result after complete scanning. 


IS 17263 : 2022 


ANNEX H 
( Table 4 ) 


DETERMINATION OF COLOR STRENGTH AND COLOR DIFFERENCE OF PRE 
COLOURED/DOPE DYED FIBRE 


H-1 INTRODUCTION 


This test method describes the determination of the 
color strength of pre colored or dope dyed fiber using 
a full scanning spectrophotometer. The color strength 
of sample is measured relative to that of a standard or 
reference sample of same type. 


H-2 MATERIAL AND EQUIPMENT 


a) Spectrophotometer of appropriate make/model. 
b) PC, Software. 
c) White and black calibration plates. 
d) Apertures — Small, medium and large. 
e) Black velvet board. 
f) Tissue paper 
H-3 PREPARATION OF SAMPLE SPECIMEN 
a) Spread the bale fibre sample (about 100 g) on a 


surface. 


b) Pick out small portions of fibre from 4 to 5 places 
at random. 


c) Thoroughly hand blend to prepare final sample. 


d) Prepare a small fibre tuft using fingers by 
repeatedly opening, drawing and parallelizing the 
fibre. 

e) Ensure a smooth plane surface avoiding crimped 
fibres on outer periphery of the tuft. 

(One can use mini carding m/c also for properly 


opening and straightening the fibre to make the 
tuft) 


H-4 PROCEDURE 


H-4.1 Switch on the spectrophotometer and PC. 


H-4.2 Select the illuminant source and observer angle 
and other settings of spectrophotometer. 


H-4.3 Select proper settings for calibration. For 
example, No. of flashes, Calibration mode 
Reflectance/Transmittance, UV inclusion, aperture 
size, illumination intensity etc. 


H-4.4 Calibrate the instrument following the 
instructions provided by instrument supplier. Complete 
calibration using the black and white reference tiles. 


16 


H-4.5 First prepare the fibre tuft using step 3 for the 
Standard/reference sample. 


H-4.6 Then prepare the specimen tuft for test sample 
as specified in H-3. 


H-4.7 Put the standard sample fibre tuft in the 
reflectance port, ensure that the aperture is completely 
covered with sample and the surface is smooth 
enough. Operate the read key and measure the values 
for L, a, b, Hue, Chroma etc. 


H-4.8 Alter the surface and take a second reading and 
note the average of both readings. 


H-4.9 Remove the standard sample and put the test 
sample at the reflectance port and measure L, a, b, 
Hue, Chroma values as per H-4.7. 


H-4.10 Rotate/alter the surface and take a second 
reading to check repeatability of results. 


H-4.11 Report the average L, a, b, Hue, Chroma 
values for sample. 


H-4.12 Delta L, Delta a, Delta b, Delta E, Delta H, 
Delta C values shall be calculated from difference 
in L, a, b, Hue, C values of standard sample and test 
sample. 


H-4.13 In the spectrophotometer the light passes 
through a monochromator that divides and diffracts 
the light much in the same way as a prism does, 
separating the entire visible spectrum of light in to 
individual colour wavelength. Reflectance values of 
the sample are measured on the spectrophotometer in 
visible region for each wavelength. 


H-4.14 Colour strength (K/S) is calculated from 
the reflectance values and directly given by the 
instrument. 


H-4.15 Note down colour strength values at the 
maximum wavelength and at all wavelengths. 


H-5 RECORD 


Record L, a, b color values, chroma, hue, delta E and 
colour strength (at all wave length and maximum 
wave length) in creel register. 


IS 17263 : 2022 


ANNEX J 
( Table 4) 
DETERMINATION OF L COLOUR VALUE AND WHITENESS INDEX 


J-1 PRINCIPLE 


Samples of yarn and staple fibre are tested for colour 
using a colorimeter instrument measuring the ‘L’ (total 
reflectance), ‘a’ (red-green), ‘b’ (yellow-blue) and ‘W° 
(whiteness) values of the fibre sample. 


J-2 APPARATUS 


a) Colorimeter instrument; 


b) Square standard tiles (white, blue, yellow, pink, 
grey and green) with the instruments; 


c) Working standard white square plate; 
d) Pressure device; 


e) Source of air at 2.10 kg/cm? + 0.35 kg/cm? 
(regulated); 


f) Sample holder with glass cover plate and clear 
plastic disc; and 


g) Air blender. 
J-3 SAFETY 


The activity involves hazard of finger cut/crush injury 
during operation of sample pressing device using air 
pressure operated metallic piston. The activity also 
involves probable injury due to breaking of glass. Carry 
out risk assessment and take control measures prior to 
starting the job. While air blending the fibre keep the lid 
tightly closed to avoid flying of fibres. 


J-4 PROCEDURE 


J-4.1 Standardization of the Unit with Working 
Standard White Tile 


Clean the working standard tile with tissue paper prior 
to use. It must be performed before reading each set of 


17 


samples. Place tile on sample port, care should be taken 
to avoid touching the surface which could change the 
reading. Compare the obtained_X, Y and Z values, with 
standard readings. If the values are not matching then 
calibrate the instrument as per instrument manual. 


J-4.2 Measurement of Lab Colour of Fibre Sample 


Prepare the test sample by proper opening of fibres 
using an air blender with clean compressed instrument 
air. Weigh 3.0 + 0.1 g of air blended sample. Place 
sample in the sample holder. Place the 0.6 cm clear 
plastic disk on the top of the sample and press down. 
The sample cup must be at least half full and the sample 
must not prevent the clear plastic disk from moving 
freely into the sample holder. Pick up the sample 
holder and look at the sample through the cover glass 
from bottom while pressing on the clear plastic disk 
by hand. If voids or dark areas are visible, rearrange 
the sample to eliminate them. Place the sample holder, 
with the clear plastic disk in place, into pressure device. 
Activate the pressure device and adjust air pressure 
2.1 kg/cm? twice and read the L, a, and b values from 
the instrument. Deactivate the pressure device. Remove 
the sample cup, reverse the sample, and place in the 
sample holder and repeat the above procedure. Report 
the results of L, a and b values as average of the two 
sets. 


J-5 CALCULATION 


Calculate whiteness index (WI) of the sample by the 
formula: 
WI=L-3b+ 3a 


Whiteness Index (WJ) is also directly obtained from the 
colorimeter instrument. 


IS 17263 : 2022 


ANNEX K 
( Table 4 ) 


DETERMINATION OF DRY HEAT SHRINKAGE OF SINGLE 
POLYESTER STAPLE FIBRE 


K-1 PRINCIPLE 


A single fibre is lightly loaded between clamps and the 
nip to nip length is measured. Without being removed 
from the clamps, the fibre is relieved of the load and 
exposed to the test environment, typically, hot air at 
specified temperature (180 + 2 °C) for a specified length 
of time (30 + 0.2 min). After re-conditioning, the fibre 
length is measured under the same loading and from the 
difference in length shrinkage is calculated. 


K-2 APPARATUS 

K-2.1 Single Fibre Shrinkage Apparatus 
K-2.2 Pretension Weight 

K-2.3 Velvet Board 

K-2.4 Lamp 

K-2.5 Forceps 


K-2.6 Oven, (180 + 2 °C), hot air, with temperature 
control. 


K-2.7 Transfer Rod, with hook for handling of cylinder. 


K-2.8 Metal Rod, with hook for lifting hot cylinder 
with sample. 


K-2.9 Heat Resistant Hand Gloves 


K-2.10 Timer, with alarm. 
K-3 SAMPLING AND CONDITIONING 


K-3.1 Take 50 to 100g of fibre sample and pick out 
10 fibre specimen at random from ten different places 
of the test sample. 


K-3.2 Condition the sample specimen in the standard 
atmosphere of 27 + 2 °C and relative humidity of 
65 + 2 percent for about 24 h (see IS 6359). Determine 
the denier of the fibre if nominal denier is not known. 


K-4 PROCEDURE 


K-4.1 Determine the denier of the fibre if the nominal 
denier is not known. Take ten fibres out at random 
from the sample to be tested as mentioned in sampling 
procedure. Keep these fibres on the specimen board. 
Select pretension weight in such a way that when it 
applied to fibre it just removes the crimps and straightens 
the fibre without stretching it. 


18 


NOTES 
1 Optimised pretension weight for 0.8 to 1.2 D is 150 mg and 
for 1.4 D and 2.0 D it is 200 mg. 


2 The pretension weights are weighed number of times to 
ensure that it is of correct mass or else use only standard 
pretension weights. 


K-4.2 Without stretching, grip one end of each fibre 
specimen with a pretension weight. Hold the other end 
of fibre with forceps and mount on the fibre clamping 
device of the shrinkage testing apparatus. Bring down 
the lower holding ring and measure the height of the 
upper clamp holding the fibre accurately on scale with 
the help of vertical sliding microscope, by coinciding 
the fibre end with the cross hair inside the eye piece. 
Record it as H.. 


K-4.3 Slide down the eye piece and coincide the lower 
end of the fibre with the cross hair. Record the height 
as H,. Record the difference between the two as L, in 
centimeter accurate to 0.01 cm. Likewise mount all 
10 specimens on the upper clamps of the shrinkage 
testing device with the cylinder kept on the platform. 
Likewise, measure and record the initial length of all 
10 specimens. Bring up the temperature resistant 
plastic ring (above the hanging length of the fibres) and 
put one arm of the hanging weight into respective holes 
to keep the fibres in relaxed condition. 


K-4.4 Lift up the sample cylinder is and put in to an 
oven heated at 180 + 2 °C for 30 min monitored by a 
timer with alarm. Take out the cylinder after 30 min and 
cool for 30 min in laboratory atmosphere. Release the 
specimens gently one by one from the holes. Measure 
the height of the lower clamps and record as H, in cm. 
The difference between H, and H, is recorded as L, in 
cm accurate to 0.01cm. 


K-5 CALCULATION 


L,-L, 


x 100 


Shrinkage, Percent = 


where 
L = Initial length, in centimeter, and 


L,= length after shrinkage, in centimeter. 


K-6 CALIBRATION 


Calibrate the scales for length measurement with 
standard vernier caliper. The oven temperature and 
timer shall be calibrated at least once in a year by 
external agency. 


IS 17263 : 2022 


ANNEX L 
( Clause 6.3 ) 
DETERMINATION OF TITANIUM DIOXIDE IN POLYMER 


L-1 GENERAL 


Titanium dioxide (TiO,) is added as a delusturant 
to minimize the luster of polyester. This method is a 
routine check to determine the TiO, percent in polymer. 
The polymer is carbonised with concentrated sulphuric 
acid and ignited at 600 + 50 °C. The sulphonated ash 
thus obtained is dissolved in fuming sulphuric acid. 
The acidic titanium solution produces a yellow colour 
complex with hydrogen peroxide. The colour species 
formed is stated to be [TiO(H,O,)]* or an analogous 
complex. The intensity of colour is measured 
spectrophotometrically at 410 nm. 


L-2 POTENTIAL ENVIORMENT ISSUES 


This can lead to pollution near the workplace area 
and health hazard in case of spillage. Sulphuric acid 
is corrosive in nature and reacts with many metals to 
form flammable hydrogen gas, which forms explosive 
mixture with air. It reacts with water to produce 
heat and toxic and corrosive fumes. Nitric acid 
dissolves some of the soil material in particular the 
carbonate-based materials. The acid will be neutralized 
to some degree with adsorption of the proton also 
occurring in clay materials. 


L-3 POTENTIAL SAFETY, OCCUPATIONAL 
HEALTH ISSUES 


Proper personal protection equipment (PPE) like 
safety goggles, nose mask and apron are required to 
be used while performing this analysis. Glassware 
is to be handled with care. Inhalation of sulphuric 
acid vapours from hot concentrated acid may injure 
lungs. Swallowing may cause injury or death. Wash 
immediately with water if contact of sulphuric acid 
is made with skin or eyes and seek medical advice. 
Inhalation of hydrogen peroxide may cause irritation 
in the respiratory tract. Skin contact of solution of 
35 percent concentration or more causes extreme 
irritation. If contacted with eye, may cause irritation 
and may results in irreversible damage. A face shield 
must be worn while analyzing the sample. 


L-4 APPARATUS 


L-4.1 Analytical Balance — Capable of weighing to 
0.1 mg. 


L-4.2 Ultraviolet Visible Spectrophotometer 
L-4.3 Silica Gel 
L-4.4 Flask Volumetric — 100 ml, 500 ml, 1 000 ml. 


19 


L-4.5 Muffle Furnace — Capable of maintaining 
temperature 700 °C to 800 °C and accepting 7 to 8 cm 
dishes. 


L-4.6 Tongs 


L-4.7 Hot Plate — Capable of being heated to 
250-300 °C. 


L-4.8 Measuring Cylinder — 10 to 50 ml capacity. 
L-4.9 Glass Beaker — 250 ml capacity. 


L-5 REAGENTS 


L-5.1 Hydrogen Peroxide (H,O,) — 30 percent 
Analytical reagent (AR)/Laboratory reagent (LR) 
grade. 


L-5.2 Sulfuric Acid (H,SO,) — concentrated, 
Analytical reagent (AR)/Laboratory reagent (LR) 
grade. 


L-5.3 Nitric Acid — Analytical reagent (AR)/General 
reagent (GR) grade. 


L-5.4 Ammonium Sulphate — Analytical reagent 
(AR)/General reagent (GR) grade. 


L-5.5 TiO, — With known purity. 
L-6 PROCEDURE 


L-6.1 Preparation of Standard Hydrogen Peroxide 
3 Percent Solution 


Dilute 50 ml of 30 percent H,O, to 500 ml with 
demineralized water. Prepare a standard file in UV 
spectrophotometer based on operating range of TiO, 
(concentration versus absorbance). 


L-7 ANALYTICAL PROCEDURE 


L-7.1 Weigh 1.5 to 2.0 g finish free yarn or polymer 
nearest to fourth decimal. Transfer to 50 ml silica 
crucible. Add 2.5 + 0.5 ml concentrated sulphuric 
acid and heat the sample on hot plate till it becomes 
carbonized. Keep the crucible in muffle furnace 
for 1 hour at 600 + 50 °C. Cool and add 10 ml 
concentrated sulphuric acid. Heat the content till 
the ash gets dissolved. Allow the contents to cool to 
room temperature. Transfer the content quantitatively 
to a 100 ml volumetric flask containing 20-30 ml 
demineralized water with washings. Add 10 ml of 
3 percent hydrogen peroxide (H,O,), and make the final 
volume with demineralized water. For full dull TiO, 
analysis, prepare solution as follows. Dilute the above 


IS 17263 : 2022 


solution by taking 10 ml of solution in 100 ml flask and 
make up with demineralized water. Multiply the results 
by 10 in final result. 


L-7.2 Prepare a reagent blank taking 12 ml H,SO, in 
about 30-40 ml demineralized water. Add 10 ml of 
3 percent hydrogen peroxide (H,O,) and make the final 
volume to 100 ml by demineralized water. Cool to 
room temperature and find the concentration at 410 nm 
on lamda 12/35 ultraviolet visible spectrophotometer 
and 10 mm quartz cells. 


L-8 CALCULATIONS 


Absorbance x Slope factor

where 
Slope factor = 10/(Slope from graph); 
X axis in graph = mg/ml as per Table 9; and 


Y axis in graph = Absorbance.’ 


L-9 STANDARD FILE PREPARATION IN 
UV SPECTROPHOTOMETER FOR TIO, 
MEASUREMENT 


L-9.1 Accurately weigh 0.25 + 0.0002 grams of TiO, 
of known purity into a clean silica dish. Cover with 
2 g of ammonium sulphate. Add 10 ml of concentrated 
sulphuric acid and 3-5 drops concentrated nitric acid. 
Heat the content to dissolve. This usually takes 10 min 
to dissolve. The resulting solution must be clear and 
transparent. Transfer the solution quantitatively into a 
1 000 ml volumetric flask and make the final volume to 
1 litre by demineralized water as “Stock TiO, solution 
(1 ml = 0.25 mg of TiO, )”. 


L-9.2 For calibration, prepare different sets of known 
standards by taking stock solution and reagent solutions 
as mentioned in Table 9 and make up final volume to 
500 ml with demineralized water. 


L-9.3 Read the absorbance using 10 mm Quartz cell at 
410 nm against reagent blank and set the file as described 
in the operating manual of the spectrophotometer. The 
calibration data will be stored automatically in the file.

Bureau of Indian Standards 


BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016 to promote harmonious 
development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of goods and attending to 
connected matters in the country. 


Copyright 


BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced in any form without 
the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use, in the course of implementing the 
standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type or grade designations. Enquiries relating to 
copyright be addressed to the Head (Publication & Sales), BIS. 


Review of Indian Standards 


Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed 
periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are 
needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards 
should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the website- 
www.bis.gov.in or www.standardsbis.in.
